shots.title: Raumpark: a second city, one level up
shots.kicker: Isometric · the city's volumes taken up one level
shots.idea: City design is also climate design, and vice versa. RAUMPARK stands for a new typology of cities in the era of the New Climatic Regime: urban expansions and densifications in the form of populated green spaces and forests above, and interlinked with, the existing city. The shot shows it with the city's own material: some blocks of the existing city take the colours of the uses (culture, health & wellbeing, residential, green areas). First their volumes are extracted: duplicated, they lift off and hover above the city. Then the Raumpark is built beneath them: the pylons rise from the street crossings and the deck spreads out along the streets. Last the volumes come down and deform into the stacked volumes on the deck, storey by storey: what the city has, taken up one level and reshaped to fit.
shots.camera: Fixed isometric, the view of the following shots; the Raumpark grows out of the district
shots.graphics: Blocks in use colours · volumes extracted and hovering · pylons · deck · volumes settling and deforming onto the deck
shots.data: Raumpark concept: pylon positions, deck outline, programme (from the research team)
shots.transition: Same camera, the model comes apart

shots.title: Layers
shots.kicker: Exploded axo · city scale to deck
shots.idea: Straight after the Raumpark has grown, the same model comes apart into its layers: the existing city stays on the ground, then the pylons over the street crossings, the deck that branches along the streets and the use solids on top lift away one after the other, thin lines marking where the pylons land. While the stack is open, one part at a time is shown in colour and everything else turns grey: first the uses, then the structure (pylons), then the deck, each with a short text block top left that describes it. Then the stack closes again, so the viewer knows what the Raumpark is made of before the studies of sun, heat and wind.
shots.camera: Isometric, the stack opens at one layer after the other
shots.graphics: Exploded layers · lines where the pylons land · one layer in colour at a time, the rest grey · text block per part (placeholder)
shots.data: 3D model of the district, split into layers
shots.transition: Same camera, the model turns grey

shots.title: Green space, housing & density
shots.kicker: Isometric · one quantity at a time, then the density
shots.idea: What the Raumpark adds, in figures. The whole model turns grey and one quantity at a time is shown in colour, with its figure top right: first the green space the district has today (its parks), then the Raumpark's green added to it (the planted deck and the green volume), so the bar for green space grows; then the residential floors, storey by storey, in the existing blocks and in the Raumpark's housing. Last the density: the existing city turns neutral and the whole Raumpark lights up in one accent, while a graph shows the floor area of the district today and with the Raumpark stacked on top, with the increase in per cent.
shots.graphics: Grey model · parks, then Raumpark green, then housing with storey lines in colour · figures as label + bar (placeholders) · density: city neutral, Raumpark in accent, bar graph today / with Raumpark, + %
shots.data: Green space today and with the Raumpark, residential floor area, population, gross floor area of the district today and with the Raumpark (from the research team; the sketch computes it from the schematic model)

shots.title: Westbahnhof: sun & shade, summer and winter
shots.idea: Same view, the Raumpark in place above the district. Two days run as time-lapses: 21 June, with the sun high on a long arc and a short shadow under the deck, then 21 December, with the sun low on a short arc and the deck's shadow stretching far across streets and courtyards. Both day arcs stay visible, so the difference reads at once.
shots.camera: Fixed isometric · time-lapse 21 June, then 21 December
shots.graphics: Summer and winter sun arcs · deck shadow
shots.data: Sun position for Vienna on 21 June and 21 December (calculated) · 3D model of the area

shots.title: Westbahnhof: heat without / with
shots.kicker: Isometric · surface heat on a summer day
shots.idea: Same view on a summer day (21 June). First the district as it is today: asphalt streets and roofs heat up most, courtyards less, the parks stay cool. Then the Raumpark fades in and the colours shift where its deck shades the streets and courtyards below: they cool down. One scale from cool blue to deep red, the same as the heat map of Vienna in the first shot.

shots.title: Window & model, side by side
shots.idea: Starts on the overview of the district with the Raumpark. The deck turns transparent and the camera pushes in on one window of a Gründerzeit house below it. Then the view out of that window fills the screen, with light and shade moving through the room, while a small isometric sun study in the corner shows the same moment with the window marked. Both run in sync, so the abstract model meets everyday experience. The window view covers one hour of a summer afternoon (21 June, 14–15 h): the sun moves along that stretch of its path in the inset, the light patch on the floor shifts and the deck’s shadow passes the window, once.
shots.camera: Overview → deck fades to transparent → push-in on one window → full-screen window view with a synced model inset
shots.graphics: Transparent deck · window highlight · model inset · shared clock
shots.data: Same sun data · one reference flat / window
shots.transition: Out of the window, the whole day of light

shots.title: Quality of sunlight & wind
shots.kicker: Isometric · sun hours over 20 March, then the wind
shots.idea: How much sun reaches the people who live here, below the Raumpark and on it. The whole of 20 March, the equinox and the usual day for daylight studies, merged into one picture: the streets, courtyards, roofs and facades of the existing city, the deck and the Raumpark’s volumes (roofs and walls, instead of their use colours) show how many hours of direct sun they get over the day, from sky blue (little) to light orange (sun all day). The shadows of the existing blocks, the deck and its volumes are all in it, so the shot shows where the new level keeps light for the city below and where it gains the best light on top. After about 8 s the sun picture gives way to the plain model and the wind, as still lines: from the west through the streets and over the deck, rising over the use volumes; behind each volume and each pylon the flow breaks up into turbulence and small eddies, showing where the Raumpark shelters and where it stirs the air.
shots.camera: Same isometric view, still; the camera drifts in slowly
shots.graphics: Sun hours on ground, roofs, facades, deck and the Raumpark’s volumes · scale · then the plain model with still wind streamlines, wakes and eddies
shots.data: Sun position for Vienna on 20 March (calculated) · wind simulation (CFD) of the area with the Raumpark · 3D model
